readings.word: יְהַֽלְלוּךָ (Ps 84:5, scan8 / printed p.2, header line 1)
readings.reason: In the enlarged snippet I can clearly see the sheva under the yod, the patah under the he and the meteg. Under the first lamed, the dots seem to have a short horizontal stroke right next to them. That stroke could be part of a hataf-patah, or it could be the he's patah or the meteg sitting close by. At the resolution I can see, I can't tell the two apart. I also can't place the second lamed's sheva with confidence, which is what I'd use to sort out which marks belong to which letter. The full-page scan is lower resolution and doesn't help.

readings.word: וַאֲהַלְלָה (Ps 145:2, scan8 / printed p.2, body line 2)
readings.vowel_under_first_lamed: undetermined: probably plain sheva, not confirmed
readings.reason: I can see the patah under the vav, the hataf-patah under the alef, the patah under the he and the qamats under the second lamed. Under the first lamed there is a two-dot mark, but the marks under this word are packed together with very little space between them. I can't rule out that a short patah bar to the right of those dots belongs to the lamed. The full-page scan is too small to settle it.

findings: I couldn't confirm plain sheva in either word to the standard needed to close this, so I've left the check open rather than accept the existing transcription by default.
I'm not reporting a discrepancy either: nothing in the images clearly shows hataf-patah. What's unresolved is the image quality, not a conflict with the transcription.
I read the images before looking at the current text, and my readings don't rely on later printings or the familiar text.

The deciding detail in both words is whether there's a patah bar touching the right side of the dots under the first lamed. Ps 84:5 is the more doubtful of the two because the he's patah and the meteg sit right next to that spot.

To close this, check that spot on a higher-resolution crop of each word (at least 4x, cropped tightly so the second lamed's mark shows too), or measure pixel spacing on the scan. I only had an image viewer in this session, so I couldn't crop or enlarge the images any further.
